source_name: Big-4 / law-firm MNB regulatory alerts (e.g. KPMG Hungary insights)
why_relevant: Advisory firms publish rapid EN-language summaries of MNB executive circulars and recommendations, often with practical deadline read-outs. Useful as a cross-check and EN-language discovery channel, never as the primary record.

Commercial regulatory-change monitoring covering 140+ jurisdictions and 1,400+ authorities, payments-focused. Relevant as a benchmark for what a paid HU feed would deliver, and as a potential licensed shortcut — but it is a vendor claim, not a verified HU-coverage fact.
Regional legal-news aggregator with a Hungary section; good for actor mapping (which firms/advisers work on which regulatory files) and for catching regulatory changes framed as deal/market news.

source_name: ELTE-OTP Kiberbiztonsági Ipari Labor (KIBERLAB) – AI Act és a pénzügyi szektor
why_relevant: Akadémiai–banki közös labor magyar nyelvű elemzései az AI Act pénzügyi alkalmazásáról; ritka, nem eladási célú hazai szakértői réteg, jó a kockázatbesorolási viták követésére.

Second commercial horizon-scanning vendor with published methodology material (obligation mapping, alerting on effective dates). Its public guides are a usable template for designing our own HU deadline tracker even if we never buy the product.

source_name: JobsGarden — HU recruitment agency (finance, IT, business administration)
why_relevant: 15+ years placing finance and IT staff in Hungary; mid-market agency whose ads reach institutions too small to run visible career portals (savings/credit institutions, PSPs, vendors) — the tail of the regulatory-hiring signal.

source_name: Katona & Partners Attorneys at Law – Hungarian payments commentary
why_relevant: Confirmed via the Mondaq Hungary finance & banking listing as a recurring contributor publishing the same payments-law article in Hungarian, English and German ('Euróval történő fizetés' / 'Payment in Euro' / 'Zahlung in Euro'). Trilingual output makes it an unusually good source for terminology mapping on payment obligations.

source_name: KávéKözlöny — plain-language summaries of each Magyar Közlöny issue
why_relevant: Issue-by-issue AI-generated plain-Hungarian summaries of the official gazette, useful purely as a fast triage signal to decide which issues merit full parsing. The site itself states the official text on magyarkozlony.hu remains authoritative; treat as untrusted for any date or obligation.

entity_name: Mastercard Hungary / mastercard.hu and Mastercard B2B newsroom
source_name: Mastercard Hungary / mastercard.hu and Mastercard B2B newsroom (Hungary instant payments)
why_relevant: Card scheme's Hungarian-language public surface; Mastercard is also a technology supplier to the Hungarian instant payment build. Useful for detecting scheme-communicated product/portfolio changes affecting Hungarian issuers (e.g. reported withdrawal of a card product from the Hungarian market).

source_name: Moneywiki regulator profile — Magyar Nemzeti Bank
why_relevant: Third-party English profile of the MNB as integrated regulator; a lightweight pointer to the supervisor's mandate and official portals. Low authority — use only for navigation, never as an evidence source.

source_name: N-Lex — EU gateway to the Hungarian national law database
why_relevant: Commission-run gateway describing and querying Hungary's national legislative database through a harmonised interface. Chiefly valuable as documentation of the Hungarian database's structure and query semantics, which helps design a robust NJT crawler, and as an alternative query path.

source_name: Pénzügyi Navigátor Tanácsadó Iroda hálózat (MNB-backed financial consumer advice network)
why_relevant: Front-line advisory network that sees consumer complaints before they reach the MNB or PBT; its guidance materials and published case themes reveal emerging retail pain points (payment fraud, complaint-handling failures) ahead of formal case statistics.

entity_name: TED Developer Docs / TED Open Data
source_name: TED Developer Docs / TED Open Data (Search API, SPARQL endpoint, bulk XML)
why_relevant: Documents the exact programmatic access routes to TED (REST search API, notice XML bulk packages, SPARQL). Turns the TED source above from manual browsing into an automatable long-term collection pipeline.

source_name: Trademagazin / Daily News Hungary / XpatLoop — qvik and merchant-payments rollout coverage
why_relevant: Retail/trade and general press covering qvik go-lives at named merchants and banks, occasionally naming the developer/technology provider behind the rollout — a merchant-side indirect route into acquiring-side supplier identities.
